submission.justification:
Sensor-T1 at 150 μm thickness achieves the best possible single-hit spatial resolution of 5.841 μm for the HL-LHC innermost pixel layer, based on comprehensive simulations across all three candidate technologies and the full thickness range (50-300 μm).

PERFORMANCE: Sensor-T1 at 150 μm delivers 5.841 μm resolution, significantly outperforming Sensor-T3 (9.067 μm, 55% worse) and Sensor-T2 (14.229 μm at optimal 100 μm thickness, 144% worse). This represents the absolute best performance across all 18 simulation combinations.

OPTIMIZATION: The 150 μm thickness represents the optimal balance for Sensor-T1's thin-pitch architecture with large signal sharing. Thinner sensors (50 μm: 6.841 μm) suffer from insufficient signal, while thicker sensors (300 μm: 8.158 μm) experience excessive lateral charge diffusion. The design shows robustness with excellent resolution (6.37-6.48 μm) maintained across the 100-200 μm range, providing manufacturing tolerance.

PHYSICAL BASIS: Sensor-T1's thin-pitch design with large signal sharing enables superior charge interpolation between pixels. At 150 μm thickness, adequate signal-to-noise is maintained while minimizing lateral charge spread, allowing precise sub-pixel position reconstruction through analog cluster centroid calculation.

RADIATION QUALIFICATION: All three candidate technologies passed radiation tolerance assessment for the innermost layer HL-LHC environment. Sensor-T1 is fully qualified for the extreme radiation conditions, supported by CO2 cooling at -35°C.

This data-driven selection achieves the project goal of "best possible single-hit spatial resolution" while meeting all operational constraints and integration requirements.
